articles.title: Microsoft Goes Down! Outlook, Teams, OpenAI & Anthropic Affected
articles.description: Microsoft 365, Outlook and Teams experienced widespread outages across the US on Thursday, November 12, affecting thousands of users. Downdetector reported over 97,000 complaints about Outlook, 38,000 about Microsoft 365 and approximately 4,500 about Teams. Microsoft acknowledged the disruption and said it was working urgently to minimize its impact. The company paused software deployments, redirected traffic away from affected infrastructure and restarted impacted servers to restore services. Although Microsoft initially announced that a Teams outage in North America had been resolved, it later warned that Microsoft 365 connectivity issues could affect users in other regions. The disruption also impacted AI services, with OpenAI reporting problems involving Microsoft connectors that affected new connections and tools. Anthropic similarly identified an issue with an upstream provider affecting its Microsoft 365 connector. The incident highlighted the widespread dependence of productivity and AI platforms on Microsoft's cloud infrastructure.

articles.title: CleanMax to invest Rs 50,000 crore in AI compute, renewable energy projects in Andhra Pradesh
articles.description: CleanMax will allocate Rs 50,000 crore towards establishing a renewable energy and AI compute facility in Andhra Pradesh. Partnering with Neysa, a 2 GW AI computing center will rise in Kurnool district, set to provide 1,000 jobs by March 2028. This ambitious plan also includes generating 3 GW of wind, 2 GW of solar, and 1 GW of hydro storage energy, transforming Andhra Pradesh's technological landscape.

articles.title: Why the AI World Will Never Be the Same
articles.description: Until this week, Jensen Huang was one of the most powerful people in the most powerful industry on earth. Now, after 33 years running Nvidia, he’s out. Ahead of our usual conversation dropping Friday, we’re bringing you a personal essay from Kevin, who has spent years covering the race to AGI and nearly made Huang a main character in his book. He explains the three central roles Huang played in the AI boom, and why he thinks the affairs alone don’t explain why Huang had to go.A note: After we recorded this episode, Reuters reported that Huang allegedly had a third affair, with a second Nvidia employee. That brings the total number of reported affairs to three.For a transcript of this episode, select the episode on npr.org/machinegods.You can watch this full episode on YouTube, Spotify or Apple Podcasts. And if you’ve got a question you want us to answer, you can drop us a comment on any of those platforms or email us at hey@machinegods.fm.

articles.title: Wall Street shakes with swings for Nvidia and oil prices but recovers most of its early losses
articles.description: NEW YORK — The US stock market shook Thursday, but it largely absorbed big swings for Nvidia and oil prices and finished with relatively modest losses. The moves suggested Wall Street sees limited fallout for the artificial intelligence industry, which carries immense influence on the market, despite the sudden fall of one of its biggest evangelists.
